description.value:
🎙 말하는 순간, 일정이 완성됩니다

"다음 주 화요일 오후 3시 강남에서 팀 회의" — 이 한 마디로 충분합니다.
PlanFlow는 음성을 AI로 분석해 날짜, 시간, 장소, 제목을 자동으로 파악하고 일정으로 저장합니다.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🚀 핵심 기능
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🎙 AI 음성 일정 입력
복잡한 타이핑 없이 말 한마디로 일정 등록. AI가 날짜·시간·장소·메모를 자동 파악합니다.

🗺 이동시간 계산 출발 알림
약속 장소까지의 실제 이동 시간을 계산해, 여유 있게 출발할 수 있도록 미리 알려드립니다.

☀️ 아침·저녁 브리핑
오늘 일정을 AI가 음성으로 브리핑해드립니다. 하루를 준비하는 가장 스마트한 방법.

📅 캘린더 연동
Google 캘린더와 연동해 기존 일정도 함께 관리하세요.

🏠 홈 위젯
마이크 버튼 하나로 홈 화면에서 바로 일정을 추가할 수 있습니다.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🔒 프라이버시 우선
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

음성은 기기 내에서만 처리됩니다. 녹음 파일이 서버로 전송되지 않으며, 텍스트 변환 후에만 AI 분석이 이루어집니다. 내 목소리는 내 기기 안에서만 머뭅니다.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
💎 PRO 얼리버드
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

지금 앱 내에서 PRO 얼리버드를 신청하시면, 유료 전환 시 특별 혜택을 드립니다.
현재 베타 기간 동안 모든 기능을 무료로 사용하실 수 있습니다.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
📬 문의 및 피드백
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

버그 신고, 기능 제안, 사용 후기는 앱 내 피드백 기능을 통해 전달해 주세요.
소중한 의견 하나하나가 PlanFlow를 만들어갑니다.

collected.note: SpeechListenOptions(onDevice: true) — STT runs on-device; raw audio is not sent to a server.

purposes.note: Transcribed voice text is sent to Supabase Edge Function 'openai-proxy', which forwards to OpenAI for schedule parsing.

linkedToUser.note: insertVoiceLog payload includes 'user_id': userId alongside 'raw_text', confirming linkage.

collected.note: location_history table stores free-text location extracted from user speech ('강남역' etc.), not raw GPS coordinates. CLARIFICATION (this pass): confirm_screen.dart:2353-2357's insertLocationHistory payload's 'location' field is literally the user's spoken/typed place name (_locationController.text, a free-text string), not a geocoded lat/lng pair and not any form of device-measured location signal. storeDataTypes='approximate_location' (Play) below is therefore an APPROXIMATE MAPPING CHOICE by this profile -- Play's own 'approximate_location' category is defined around coarse device-derived location (e.g. IP-based, cell-tower), which is not quite what this is (a user-typed place name string). No better-fitting Play data-type code was found in this profile's review; flagging the mapping as approximate rather than asserting it is the objectively correct category.

CORRECTION (2nd pass, widened evidence range to 222-275): the immediately-prior note in this node was itself wrong to say Google never receives coordinates and to call docs/privacy-audit-2026-08-04.md:41 stale/inaccurate on the vendor -- that verdict is withdrawn. Directly read: confirm_screen.dart:2636-2647 (getLastKnownLocation() -> estimateWithMapApis(originLat/Lng, destinationLat/Lng)) -> travel_time_buffer_service.dart:222-248 (estimateWithMapApis) -> map_service.dart:53-90 (getTravelMinutes) tries Tmap first (_tryTmapDuration, raw GPS lat/lng in the request body) then Naver (_tryNaverDuration, raw GPS lat/lng; Naver call is routed through a proxy per lib/core/env.dart's AppEnv.naverMapProxyUrl, used at map_service.dart:38/273, rather than calling Naver directly from the client). If BOTH Tmap and Naver return null, travel_time_buffer_service.dart:264-271 falls back to estimateWithGoogleMaps(origin: '$originLat,$originLng', destination: '$destinationLat,$destinationLng') -- these are coordinate strings, not addresses, so in this fallback branch Google Distance Matrix DOES receive raw GPS coordinates. So docs/privacy-audit-2026-08-04.md:41's claim ('Google Maps Distance Matrix API, 출발/도착 좌표만 전송') is accurate for this fallback path, just incomplete (it omits that Tmap/Naver are tried first). Net: three vendors can receive precise GPS coordinates depending on availability -- Tmap (primary), Naver (secondary, via proxy), Google (fallback only when both Tmap and Naver fail). ENHANCED (this pass): transit mode only attempts Naver (map_service.dart:60-61, mode==transit → const <MapTravelProvider>[Naver]), skipping Tmap entirely. Additionally, estimateWithMapApis accepts a skipRemote parameter (travel_time_buffer_service.dart:233); when true, the function returns early with a local estimate (line 235-241) without making any remote API calls to any vendor. decisionRequired: PRECISE_LOCATION_COLLECTION.

exportEvent() builds an HTTP PUT request to sync event data to Naver CalDAV when the user enables the integration. Also confirmed the primary storage path: event_repository.dart:535 declares _tableName='events', the Supabase table events/calendar entries are persisted independent of the optional CalDAV sync. CLARIFICATION (2026-09-11): the evidence list reflects only off-device calendar collection sources: Naver CalDAV sync (lib/services/naver_caldav_service.dart:1740,1762) and Supabase server-side event persistence (event_repository.dart:535). CORRECTION (2026-09-11, HIGH-3): the prior claim in this note that Android device-calendar read/write is categorically 'not off-device data collection' was wrong for the import path. lib/services/device_calendar_service.dart's MethodChannelDeviceCalendarGateway (checkCalendarPermission:237, requestCalendarPermission:246, upsertDeviceCalendarEvent:280) only gates permission and, via upsertDeviceCalendarEvent, writes PlanFlow's own events OUT to the device calendar (export, not collection) -- permission check/request alone is not collection either. However, device_calendar_service.dart's importNaverEvents() (declared line 355) reads the device's local calendar via _gateway.listDeviceCalendarEvents (line 406) and, for each event, calls _importSingleNaverEvent (call site line 449, declared line 486), which at line 556 calls _eventRepository.upsertEventBySourceExternalId(eventModel); _eventRepository resolves to EventRepository.supabase() by default (getter at line 327-328), so imported device-calendar events ARE persisted server-side to Supabase. That import-then-upsert path is off-device data collection and is now included in the evidence list above. importNaverEvents() is invoked from lib/services/calendar_auto_sync_service.dart:245 (automatic sync) and lib/screens/settings/settings_screen.dart:837 (manual import).

shared.note: Group feature shares calendar/event data with other group members. requiresHumanAuthority=true: whether this qualifies for Play's user-initiated-sharing exemption under Data Safety needs a human policy call, not an automated collection/no-collection answer. STOREDATA_TYPES NOTE: the storeDataTypes value 'other_user_generated_content' is an approximate mapping; the engine vocabulary does not have a calendar-specific code.

collected.note: Supabase Auth-based account with deleteAccount() Edge Function call.

linkedToUser.note: CORRECTION: prior note relied solely on docs/privacy-audit-2026-08-04.md:45's claim that PII is not configured for Crashlytics. Direct code read contradicts that claim: feedback_repository.dart:375 calls crashlytics.setCustomKey('feedback_user_id', userId), attaching the app's user id to Crashlytics reports on feedback submission. confidence=MEDIUM (single call site confirmed; did not exhaustively audit every setCustomKey call across the codebase).

collected.note: Group event comments (group_event_comments table) are stored and shared among group members.

shared.note: requiresHumanAuthority=true: whether user-initiated group-comment sharing qualifies for a Data Safety sharing exemption needs a human policy call.

collected.note: The AD_ID permission (AndroidManifest.xml:4) is a capability declaration, not collection proof, and it was restored by commit aaf1bfed (git log verified 2026-09-11: 'feat(rc): voice-conv keys + restore AD_ID permission'). ad_service.dart:491 calls MobileAds.instance.initialize(), but that call is itself gated by ad_service.dart:423's `if (!RemoteConfigService.rewardedAdEnabled) { ... }` check, so whether AD_ID is actually collected in production depends on the live Firebase Remote Config value for rewardedAdEnabled, which was not read back in this pass -- value is UNKNOWN, not a confirmed true. Also see android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:27-29 (ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID, the Android 13+ Privacy Sandbox successor permission), which is likewise a capability declaration only.

purposes.note: MobileAds.instance.initialize() (ad_service.dart:491) is only reached when RemoteConfigService.rewardedAdEnabled is true (ad_service.dart:423) -- the live production Remote Config value was not read back, so whether the 'advertising' purpose is actually active is UNKNOWN.

shared.note: DERIVED from AdMob's publicly documented data-sharing behavior for rewarded-ad serving (vendor docs, not a direct HTTP-call-site read). Left as UNKNOWN/null pending decisionRequired: ANDROID_AD_ID_SHARING, since the runtime activation itself is gated by Remote Config (see collected/purposes notes) and the declaration choice is still open.

collected.note: NEW node (this pass). firebase_remote_config (pubspec.yaml:24) and firebase_crashlytics are both present, and remote_config_service.dart calls FirebaseRemoteConfig.instance (line 58) and fetchAndActivate() (line 225), with Firebase.initializeApp at line 89; main.dart also wires FirebaseCrashlytics.instance in several places and calls RemoteConfigService.initialize() at line 227. Per Firebase SDK vendor documentation, any installed Firebase SDK component (Remote Config, Crashlytics, etc.) auto-generates and transmits a Firebase Installation ID (FID) to Google's backend at init/fetch time -- this was not verified by capturing an outbound network call in this pass, so source=DERIVED/confidence=LOW rather than CODE_EVIDENCE/HIGH. Engine vocabulary source: E:\FluxStudio\tools\flux-release\store\fluxstore\privacy\sdk_data_types.json's firebase_remote_config entry maps android->["device_or_other_ids"], with its own note explicitly identifying this as 'Firebase Installation ID (per-install identifier used to fetch remote config values)'.
onDevice: true is set in the shared (non-platform-specific) stt_service.dart code path.

usedForTracking.note: Sent only to first-party Supabase Edge Function / OpenAI for app functionality, not for cross-app tracking.

collected.note: Same shared Dart code path as Android; free-text location, not GPS coordinates. CLARIFICATION (this pass): the 'location' value is the user's spoken/typed place name string (_locationController.text via confirm_screen.dart:2353-2357), not a geocoded coordinate or device-measured signal. storeDataTypes='COARSE_LOCATION' (App Store) below is an APPROXIMATE MAPPING CHOICE, same caveat as android.dataTypes.location -- Apple's COARSE_LOCATION category is defined around device-derived approximate position, which is not quite what a user-typed place name is; no better-fitting App Store category was identified in this pass.

CODE_EVIDENCE: shared iOS path sends raw GPS coordinates to Tmap/Naver and Google fallback for travel-time estimation. The decision to disclose this as precise location remains a human App Privacy/legal confirmation.

CORRECTION (prior note in this node was wrong): two distinct things need to be kept separate. (1) Device calendar PERMISSION (not collection): AppDelegate.swift's 'requestCalendarPermission' channel handler (line 93 dispatch, 190-209 implementation) calls EKEventStore().requestFullAccessToEvents on iOS 17+ (or requestAccess(to: .event) pre-17) -- a real runtime EventKit permission prompt, invoked from lib/screens/onboarding/permission_onboarding_screen.dart:358 via app_permission_service.dart's 'planflow/ios_permissions' channel. This justifies the NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription/NSCalendarsUsageDescription Info.plist strings but is NOT itself data collection. (2) Actual EventKit device-calendar READ/WRITE: lib/services/device_calendar_service.dart's MethodChannelDeviceCalendarGateway (checkCalendarPermission line 237, requestCalendarPermission line 246, upsertDeviceCalendarEvent line 280) all early-return false/no-op unless defaultTargetPlatform == TargetPlatform.android -- it talks to the Android-only 'planflow/android_permissions' MethodChannel (MainActivity.kt CalendarContract), so on iOS no code path actually reads or writes the device's EventKit calendar events. What IS collected on iOS: the app's own schedules (created via voice/manual entry) are persisted server-side in Supabase's 'events' table (event_repository.dart:535, SupabaseEventRepository, platform-shared code), which is collection of user-generated event content, not device-calendar access. collected=true reflects this server-side event storage, not EventKit reads. Note: iOS permission request (AppDelegate.swift:93, 190-209) and Android device-calendar access (device_calendar_service.dart:237, 246, 280) are documented separately in the iOS and Android private notes, not in collected.evidence.

linkedToUser.note: CORRECTION, same basis as the android crashData.linkedToUser fix: feedback_repository.dart:375 is shared (non-platform-specific) Dart code that calls crashlytics.setCustomKey('feedback_user_id', userId) on both platforms.

evidence: User-provided Build24 runtime evidence: rcFetch=true, iosUnit=valueRemote, RewardedAd.load called
collected.note: Current source/runtime evidence proves the Google Mobile Ads SDK is invoked on iOS. Google's current disclosure says the SDK may collect advertising data, device identifiers and interactions. This is a source-plus-provider derived expected App Privacy answer; cross-app tracking/IDFA remains UNKNOWN pending ATT/runtime and business confirmation.

usedForTracking.note: ATT/IDFA tracking answer is UNKNOWN: no requestTrackingAuthorization/AppTrackingTransparency/ATTrackingManager call was found in lib/, while NSUserTrackingUsageDescription exists in Info.plist. Do not mark tracking false without product/legal confirmation.

collected.note: The audited file/share path accepts ICS calendar files only; no photo-library collection path was found. Reconfirm if future imports expand beyond ICS.

NEW node (this pass), iOS counterpart of privacy.android.dataTypes.firebaseInstallationId -- same shared Dart evidence (firebase_remote_config in pubspec.yaml:24, remote_config_service.dart's FirebaseRemoteConfig.instance at line 58, Firebase.initializeApp at line 89, fetchAndActivate at line 225, main.dart's FirebaseCrashlytics.instance wiring and RemoteConfigService.initialize() at line 227). Per Firebase SDK vendor documentation, an installed Firebase SDK component auto-generates and transmits a Firebase Installation ID (FID) at init/fetch time; not verified via a captured outbound network call in this pass, so source=DERIVED/confidence=LOW. Engine vocabulary source: sdk_data_types.json's firebase_remote_config entry maps ios->["DEVICE_ID"], with its own note identifying this as the Firebase Installation ID used to fetch remote config values.

tracking.note: Top-level tracking summary (iOS ATT). NSUserTrackingUsageDescription key is present in Info.plist (line 32) — this is a tracking SIGNAL, not proof of absence or presence. No ATT request code found in lib/ (0 matches for requestTrackingAuthorization/AppTrackingTransparency/ATTrackingManager) and 0 SKAdNetworkItems declared, but ios/Runner/Info.plist:7 also declares GADApplicationIdentifier, so the native Google Mobile Ads SDK may auto-initialize and collect advertising identifiers on iOS regardless of the Dart-level gate — whether that constitutes ATT-scoped tracking is UNKNOWN. decisionRequired: IOS_ADS_TRACKING_ANSWER. Android AD_ID-based ad personalization is separately governed by UMP consent in lib/services/ad_consent_service.dart, feeding the Play Data Safety 'advertising' purpose declaration, not this iOS ATT field.

android.note: CORRECTION: the prior note here was copied from content.ageRating.ios ('사용자가 App Store 제출 시 연령 등급 설정을 했다고 진술') -- that is an App Store (iOS) statement and has no bearing on Google Play's separate IARC content-rating questionnaire. No Play-specific age-rating statement or readback exists for android; value is UNKNOWN pending a Play Console IARC questionnaire readback.

ios.note: CORRECTION: confidence was MEDIUM while value is null -- inconsistent. 사용자가 App Store 제출 시 '연령 등급 설정'을 했다고 진술했으나 구체 등급 값 자체는 미확인이므로 value=null과 일관되게 confidence=UNKNOWN으로 정정.

contentRights.note: 사용자가 PlanFlow는 콘텐츠 권한 질문에 '아니요'라고 진술. REBUTTAL note (this pass): the app displays third-party map content via pubspec.yaml:21 (google_maps_flutter) and lib/screens/location/location_picker_screen.dart:593 (GoogleMap widget) and imports calendar/event data from Google Calendar (lib/services/calendar_sync_service.dart:2001, events.list API call inside _fetchGoogleEventsForCalendar, feeding syncGoogleCalendar at line 404) and Naver CalDAV (lib/services/naver_caldav_service.dart:861 getEvents() issuing a REPORT request at line 950 via _queryEvents). CORRECTION (2026-09-11, MEDIUM-1): the previously cited naver_caldav_service.dart:1740,1762 are exportEvent()'s outbound PUT request (PlanFlow pushing its own events out to Naver), not an import/third-party-content-ingestion path, and have been replaced with the actual import citations above. Whether displaying/importing this third-party-sourced data counts as 'using third-party content' under the store's specific question wording was not re-litigated in this pass; confidence lowered to LOW to reflect this unresolved rebuttal. CLARIFICATION: lib/services/map_service.dart의 경로 API(Tmap, Naver, Google Distance Matrix)는 이동 소요시간(분)만 반환하는 계산 API이며, 지도 콘텐츠 표시의 근거가 아니다.

ugc.note: Group event comments are user-generated content, with no moderation capability found: grep for report|block|신고|차단 across lib/features/groups (case-insensitive) returned 3 matches, all unrelated to content moderation -- group_repository.dart:41,198 and group_detail_screen.dart:734 all describe blocking the last group leader from leaving the group, not reporting/blocking users or comments. No report/block/flag UI or backend function for group_event_comments was found. This is an Apple Guideline 1.2 (UGC) risk: apps with user-generated content typically must provide a mechanism to report objectionable content and block abusive users. decisionRequired: UGC_MODERATION.

chat.note: No 1:1/group chat screens or SDKs found: pubspec.yaml dependencies block (lines 9-51) contains no chat/messaging SDK, confirmed by python -m fluxstore impact --project-root E:\FluxStudio\PlanFlow --json (SDK fingerprint componentCount=7, all 7 are non-chat: google_mobile_ads/firebase_crashlytics/firebase_remote_config/firebase_core/supabase_flutter/google_sign_in/speech_to_text). glob for chat*.dart under lib/ returned 0 files; grep -rli 'chat' lib/ found only lib/screens/home/home_widgets.dart:417 and lib/widgets/planflow_voice_fab.dart:70, both Icons.chat_bubble_outline icon usage, not a chat feature. Group commentary is classified under 'ugc', not chat. requiresHumanAuthority=true: this negative finding rests on absence of evidence (no dedicated chat SDK/screens), not a positive rule-out -- supabase_flutter is a general-purpose backend and could in principle carry an ad-hoc user-to-user messaging table this pass did not enumerate every table for. A human should confirm no such Supabase table exists before treating this as final.

health.note: No health-related SDK or feature found in pubspec.yaml/lib.

finance.note: No finance/payments SDK or feature found (no in_app_purchase dependency).

gambling.note: No gambling-related feature or SDK found.

android.note: MobileAds.instance.initialize() (ad_service.dart:491) plus the AD_ID permission (AndroidManifest.xml:4) confirm the app is CAPABLE of running rewarded ads on Android, but ad_service.dart:423 gates that call behind `RemoteConfigService.rewardedAdEnabled`, whose live production value was not read back in this pass -- whether ads are actually active is UNKNOWN, not a confirmed true. See privacy.android.dataTypes.androidAdvertisingId for the same gating.

ios.note: iOS rewarded ads are active in source when Remote Config provides a valid rewarded_ad_unit_id_ios; the current iOS readback identifies app 6806790412. AdMob availability/processing is applicable. ATT/IDFA tracking remains a separate UNKNOWN human decision.

medicalClaims.note: PlanFlow is a scheduling/calendar app; no medical/health-claims feature or copy was checked in this pass. Left UNKNOWN rather than assumed false pending an explicit review of store-listing copy for any health/medical claims language.

encryption.note: ios/Runner/Info.plist:9 declares the ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption key (value not independently re-read in this pass; see decisionsRequired.EXPORT_COMPLIANCE_CONFIRM which already cites this same key as false). Whether that declared value is an accurate, human-confirmed export-compliance statement (vs. an unreviewed default) is UNKNOWN -- linked to decisionRequired: EXPORT_COMPLIANCE_CONFIRM. SCOPE NOTE (this pass): the store-profile.v1 schema's content.encryption node has no per-platform (android/ios) split (unlike content.ads/monetization.model which do) -- it is a single value for the whole app. The only evidence gathered is iOS-specific (Info.plist's ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption has no Android/Play equivalent; Play's Data Safety encryption-in-transit question is answered per data type, not as one binary app-level flag). This node should be read as an iOS-export-compliance-only judgment; it does not represent an Android finding, and confidence/value should not be assumed to generalize to Android's separate encryption-in-transit declarations (see the per-data-type encryptedInTransit field in androidDataType, currently unused/unset for any Android data type in this profile).

A separate real blocker remains: the current live 7-inch image exposes real schedule/business content, and both live tablet images contain system/DeX chrome and use 16:10 rather than Google's recommended large-screen 16:9/9:16 formats. Replace or remove those live optional assets in a separately authorized Play metadata change.

acceptedFingerprints.note: 재생성(2026-09-11, 플랫폼 스코프 fix): 이전 버전은 PERMISSION/SDK/MONETIZATION/STORE_PROFILE/SCREENSHOT_FEATURE를 Android/iOS 구분 없이 합산해, iOS 전용 변경(Info.plist NS*UsageDescription 등)이 android impact의 PRIVACY_CHANGE로 잘못 잡히는 결함이 있었다(명세 §36 위반). fluxstore.fingerprint.compute_all(..., platform="android")로 재생성했고, 문서에 platformScoped:true를 기록했다 — 플랫폼 스코프가 아닌 기준선은 이제 impact/plan 로더가 거부한다. 소스=18075eda 트리(Play production 1.1.1(164) completed 확인, readback 2026-09-11), 가정은 이전 버전과 동일(오케스트레이터가 업로드 직후 버전 커밋을 남기는 구조이므로 트리 동일성 가정, byte-identical 빌드머신 검증은 아님). STORE_PROFILE/SCREENSHOT_FEATURE는 이 커밋 트리에 config/store 자체가 없어 현재(2026-09-11) profile/screenshot-lineage로 android 스코프 계산 — 즉 두 카테고리는 '지금부터'의 android 드리프트만 추적한다(이전 버전과 동일한 결정, null 처리 시 매번 METADATA_CHANGE 노이즈가 나는 문제를 피하기 위함).
